title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Criminals used AI-generated video and text to impersonate a real immigration attorney on social media, creating hundreds of fake profiles to solicit payment from immigrants seeking legal services. The scam operated without human intermediaries to verify the attorney's identity or legitimacy of the offers. This is an impersonation attack enabled by generative AI tools that can create convincing digital replicas of real people.

The scheme exploited a gap between where these fraudulent profiles existed, on mainstream social media platforms, and where identity verification would normally occur. Social media platforms did not block the accounts until an anti-piracy company manually identified and reported them. Catching this earlier would have required either platform-level detection of coordinated inauthentic behavior or verification systems that confirmed the identity of accounts claiming to offer professional services.

It is not established whether the social media platforms had prior notice of these specific profiles or what capabilities they deploy to detect AI-generated impersonation at scale.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of artificial intelligence scammers who are impersonating him to defraud vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos showing a digital version of Leal offering fraudulent immigration services, including US residency assistance for $2,200. The scheme began escalating dramatically in recent months, with scammers directing victims through social media to WhatsApp contact numbers, where they send fake contracts and request payment through digital payment apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App.

Leal first discovered the fraud when potential clients began calling his office last October, but the problem has spiraled significantly in the past three months. His firm hired an online anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake social media profiles, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scammers' origins. He is warning immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to avoid those requesting immediate payment through digital payment platforms.
